title: Free bisimplex projective resolutions and pointwise cone contractions
statement:
Let $\Delta$ have objects $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, $n\geq0$, and monotone maps, and put $I=\Delta\times\Delta$. Work with abelian groups in a universe containing the small category $I$. Set $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathrm{Ab})$ and $R_i(j)=\mathbf Z[\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)]$, the free abelian group of finite integral sums of arrows, with postcomposition as structure maps. Then $\mathcal E$ is abelian [def-sp-abelian], and kernels, cokernels, epimorphisms and exactness are computed pointwise. There is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(R_i,F)\cong F(i)$ sending $f$ to $f_i([1_i])$, with inverse $x\mapsto([\alpha]\mapsto F(\alpha)x)$. Every $R_i$ and every finite sum of these functors is projective, meaning that every map from it lifts through every epimorphism. Moreover $\bigoplus_{(i,x),\,x\in F(i)}R_i\to F$, with generator $1_i$ sent to $x$, is an epimorphism from a projective object; thus $\mathcal E$ has enough projectives.

Define augmented nonnegative chain complexes by
$$P_n=R_{(n,n)},\qquad Q_n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}R_{(a,b)}.$$
The boundary of $P$ is alternating precomposition by the diagonal cofaces. The boundary of $Q$ on the $(a,b)$ summand is alternating precomposition by first-variable cofaces plus $(-1)^a$ times that in the second variable, omitting a direction of degree zero. Both augment to the constant functor $\underline{\mathbf Z}$ by sending each vertex to $1$. These are projective resolutions: their terms are projective and their augmented sequences are exact.

More explicitly, for every $p,q\geq0$, use the unnormalized free string complexes $U(p),U(q),V(p,q)$ of [lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary], retaining repeated vertices. Evaluation gives $P(p,q)=V(p,q)$ and $Q(p,q)=\operatorname{Tot}(U(p)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}U(q))$. Prepending $(0,0)$ defines maps $h_n:P_n(p,q)\to P_{n+1}(p,q)$. If $e:\mathbf Z\to P_0(p,q)$ selects that vertex and $E=e\epsilon$ in degree zero and zero otherwise, then $\partial h+h\partial=1-E$. Prepending $0$ gives $h_p,h_q$ and degree-zero projections $E_p,E_q$ for $U(p),U(q)$. On a tensor with $u\in U(p)_a$ put
$$H(u\otimes v)=h_pu\otimes v+(-1)^a E_pu\otimes h_qv.$$
Then $\partial H+H\partial=1-E_p\otimes E_q$. Both degree-zero augmentations are surjective. The contractions are pointwise and are not asserted to be natural in $(p,q)$.

Agent-formulated free-abelian product-simplex and tensor contractions and representable projectivity, extracted from returned proof steps 1–3; the tag supplies the simplex contraction motivation, not the entire statement.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact] to $\mathcal C=I^{\mathrm{op}}$: its presheaves are the covariant diagrams $\mathcal E$. Thus $\mathcal E$ is abelian and kernels and cokernels are pointwise. Concretely, for $f:F\to G$ the groups $G(j)/f_j(F(j))$, with induced structure maps, form its cokernel. Hence $f$ is epic exactly when these quotients vanish: if its cokernel is nonzero, its quotient map is a nonzero map killed by $f$; conversely, componentwise surjectivity permits cancellation of $f$ against any two natural transformations. Kernels and images are likewise the subgroups $\ker f_j$ and $f_j(F(j))$ with induced maps. Consequently exactness is both preserved and detected pointwise, rather than merely preserved by evaluation.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written pointwise categorical argument (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: For $x\in F(i)$ define $T_x(j)(\sum_\alpha n_\alpha[\alpha])=\sum_\alpha n_\alpha F(\alpha)x$. The finite, unique expression in the free basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] makes this a homomorphism. For $\beta:j\to k$, $F(\beta)T_x(j)[\alpha]=F(\beta\alpha)x=T_x(k)R_i(\beta)[\alpha]$, proving naturality. Conversely, naturality of $f:R_i\to F$ at $\alpha:i\to j$ gives $f_j[\alpha]=F(\alpha)f_i[1_i]$. These formulas prove the two inverse identities. Postcomposition by $F\to G$ sends $x$ to its image in $G(i)$; precomposition induced by $i'\to i$ sends $x'\in F(i')$ to $F(i'\to i)x'$. Thus the bijection is natural in both variables.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written free-generator calculation of the Yoneda bijection (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: For an epimorphism $a:F\to G$ and $t:R_i\to G$, step 1 makes $a_i$ surjective. Choose $y\in F(i)$ with $a_i(y)=t_i[1_i]$. The map $T_y$ of step 2 lifts $t$, since both composites have that value on $[1_i]$. For any small family $(i_s)_{s\in S}$, construct $A=\bigoplus_s R_{i_s}$ pointwise: $A(j)$ consists of finite sums of basis symbols $(s,[\alpha:i_s\to j])$, and structure maps postcompose $\alpha$. Its coproduct property follows by restricting a homomorphism to these summands and summing on each finite support. Lifting a map $A\to G$ now amounts to choosing such a $y_s$ for every summand and using this property. Choice on the set $S$ supplies them. This proves projectivity for every such coproduct, including finite and empty ones, without assuming that arbitrary products preserve epimorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written explicit lifting argument for representables and their sums (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: For $S=\{(i,x):i\in I,\ x\in F(i)\}$ the coproduct is small in the stated universe. Its maps $T_x:R_i\to F$ assemble to $a:A\to F$. For $z\in F(j)$, the generator $[1_j]$ in the $(j,z)$ summand maps to $z$, so every $a_j$ is surjective. Step 1 makes $a$ epic and step 3 makes $A$ projective. Thus there are enough projectives. Small coproducts also exist abstractly by [lem-weil-pbc-functor-abelian-colimits], applied to the small category $I$ and to $\mathrm{Ab}$; the explicit finite-support construction above gives the coproduct used here.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written enough-projectives construction (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: At $(p,q)$, an arrow $([n],[n])\to([p],[q])$ is exactly a weakly increasing string of $n+1$ pairs; thus the free basis identifies $P_n(p,q)$ with $V(p,q)_n$ of [lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary]. Precomposing a diagonal coface deletes that pair. Similarly a basis arrow $([a],[b])\to([p],[q])$ is a pair of strings $(u,v)$, giving $R_{(a,b)}(p,q)=U(p)_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}U(q)_b$ by the free-on-pairs identification in that node's statement. The two coface sums give precisely $D(u\otimes v)=\partial u\otimes v+(-1)^a u\otimes\partial v$, with degree-zero directions omitted. These identifications respect postcomposition and both vertex augmentations.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written basis identifications of the two evaluated complexes (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: The displayed boundaries define augmented complexes. For an alternating deletion differential, every deletion of positions $i<j$ occurs twice in $\partial^2$, with signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, hence cancels, including repeated entries. For the tensor differential the two mixed terms have coefficients $(-1)^{a-1}$ and $(-1)^a$, and the unmixed terms are zero by the same deletion calculation; if either degree is zero, its differential and both corresponding mixed contributions are absent. On a degree-one string the augmentation sends its boundary to $1-1=0$. Coface precomposition commutes with postcomposition, so the boundaries and augmentations are natural transformations. Finally $P_n$ is representable-free and $Q_n$ is a sum of $n+1$ representable-free functors, and step 3 proves their projectivity.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written square-zero and augmentation calculations (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: On a basis string $z=(z_0,\ldots,z_n)$ of $V(p,q)$ define $hz=((0,0),z_0,\ldots,z_n)$. The coordinatewise minimum makes this a legal weakly increasing string even if $z_0=(0,0)$. For $n>0$, deleting the prepended vertex gives $z$, while deletion at position $i+1$ has sign $(-1)^{i+1}$ and is $h$ of the deletion at $i$ of $z$. Therefore $\partial hz=z-h\partial z$. For $n=0$, $\partial h(z_0)=(z_0)-((0,0))=(1-e\epsilon)(z_0)$. By linearity these identities give $\partial h+h\partial=1-E$ in every degree. They use the unnormalized bases of [lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary], so no repeated simplex has been set to zero.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written minimum-vertex contraction of the product simplex (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: The identical calculation for an ordinary string, replacing $(0,0)$ by $0$, gives $\partial h_p+h_p\partial=1-E_p$ and $\partial h_q+h_q\partial=1-E_q$. Here $E_p$ sends every degree-zero vertex to $(0)$ and is zero in positive degrees. Thus $\partial E_p=0$: its nonzero outputs have degree zero. Also $E_p\partial=0$: only the boundary of a degree-one string can contribute, and its two vertices have opposite coefficients. The same assertions hold for $E_q$. In particular both $E_p,E_q$ are chain maps, with no assumption about commuting with $h_p,h_q$.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written single-simplex contraction and degree-zero chain projections (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: For homogeneous $u\in U(p)_a$, $v\in U(q)_b$, split the required $H$ into $A(u\otimes v)=h_pu\otimes v$ and $B(u\otimes v)=(-1)^aE_pu\otimes h_qv$. Expanding $DA+AD$, the mixed terms are $(-1)^{a+1}h_pu\otimes\partial v$ and $(-1)^ah_pu\otimes\partial v$, which cancel. What remains is $(\partial h_p+h_p\partial)u\otimes v=(1-E_p)u\otimes v$. For $B$, it vanishes unless $a=0$. If $a=0$, $DB+BD=E_pu\otimes(\partial h_q+h_q\partial)v=E_pu\otimes(1-E_q)v$. If $a=1$, the only possible term is $E_p\partial u\otimes h_qv=0$ by step 8; if $a>1$ every term is zero by degree. This gives $DB+BD=E_p\otimes(1-E_q)$ in all cases. Adding proves $DH+HD=1-E_p\otimes E_q$, exactly with the sign and degree-zero convention stated in the item.

source.place: Tag 08Q3, example-simplex-contractible; agent-written expansion of the tensor contraction with the Koszul signs (the tag motivates the minimum-vertex contraction only)

proof.text: Write $C$ for either evaluated complex and $T$ for its displayed contraction. In positive degree, the projection in $DT+TD=1-E$ is zero, so every cycle $z$ equals $DTz$, proving exactness. In degree zero, a vector $z$ with $\epsilon z=0$ has $Ez=0$, again giving $z=DTz$. Each boundary has augmentation zero by step 6. Finally $\epsilon e=1$ for $P$, and $\epsilon((0)\otimes(0))=1$ for $Q$, so the augmentations are surjective. This proves exactness of both augmented sequences at every $(p,q)$; the pointwise kernels and cokernels of [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact] give exactness in $\mathcal E$. With step 6 this proves both are projective resolutions. None of this needs the contractions to be natural: for example a monotone map $[0]\to[1]$ with value $1$ sends the chosen vertex $0$ to $1$, not to the chosen vertex $0$.
